notes:
Account context
- Northstar Bank (regulated). Platform team building internal GenAI capabilities (ops support + policy summarization + document Q&A). Current approach is a mix of internal GPU clusters + vendor APIs; they want a single inference platform with predictable operations.

Why they care about Runtime LTS (key theme)
- They have strict change management (CAB) and a low tolerance for "surprise" regressions. They explicitly asked for an LTS channel with:
  - Stable kernel + scheduling behavior (no experimental heuristics landing mid-stream)
  - Predictable patch cadence (monthly preferred; out-of-band only for security/Sev1)
  - Explicit backport eligibility rubric (security + Sev1/Sev2 only; minimal diffs)
  - Enterprise-grade release notes (categorized changes + known issues + perf notes)
- Quote from 2/6 call (paraphrase): "We can’t upgrade every few weeks just to keep things running. Give us a stable line and tell us exactly what changes."

Deployment + data residency constraints
- Deployment model: Redwood Private in their AWS VPC (US regions only). They want network egress tightly controlled; no cross-region failover by default.
- Data residency: "US-only processing" requirement; they requested contractual language that inference requests and logs remain in US regions.
- Key management: customer-managed KMS required. They asked about HSM support as a future option; for now KMS integration is acceptable.
- Logging/retention: audit logs required; retention controls required (they referenced 30/90/180 day tiers depending on log type). They asked if Redwood can support "no prompt logging" mode except explicit debug windows.

Change control expectations
- They require advance notice for planned changes:
  - Standard patch releases: 10 business day notice preferred (at minimum 5 days) + release notes at publish time.
  - Emergency security patches: allowed out-of-band with shorter notice, but must include: CVE details, impact statement, mitigations, and clear "mandatory" designation.
- CAB requires: compatibility matrix, rollback steps, and validation checklist. They asked Redwood to provide "upgrade notes" per patch (even if no action required).

Patch cadence + SLAs (what they asked for)
- Requested: monthly LTS patches + security patch SLA.
  - They suggested: critical CVE fix in <= 72 hours with guidance; high-severity <= 7 days.
  - They also asked for clarity on what is considered "critical" (CVSS threshold + exploitability + customer exposure).
- They will not accept a plan that requires frequent runtime upgrades outside the LTS line.

Performance / reliability requirements (high level)
- Latency target: p95 < 1.5s for typical internal chat requests (varies by model; they understand model-dependent).
- They care more about variance/predictability than absolute best throughput. They explicitly asked for perf regression gates on LTS patches.
- They asked about "graceful degradation" when capacity constrained (fallback models) but want this to be an explicit, opt-in policy and logged for audit.

Procurement timeline / commercial notes
- Procurement timeline as of 3/20:
  - Legal review in progress; target signature by late April / early May.
  - InfoSec needs final answers on provenance/SBOM and written LTS patch policy language.
- Packaging: likely Private platform fee + Dedicated reserved capacity (pilot to prod). They asked for pricing to be tied to committed throughput rather than purely usage during initial rollout.

Open questions / asks for Redwood
- Provide customer-facing LTS commitment language (support window, patch cadence, backport policy summary, security patch SLA). (Avery coordinating with Release Eng + Security)
- Confirm artifact verification details for Private (checksums/provenance; SBOM status). They asked for a step-by-step doc and whether signatures are supported.
- Confirm how LTS interacts with Private installer/Helm pinning (they want explicit examples: pin to 1.18.1-lts; rollback to 1.18.0-lts).
- Provide a sample "slower-change" LTS release note (they want to see categories, known issues, compatibility matrix, mitigations).

Internal routing
- This deal is explicitly blocked on LTS commitment. Liam (SE) and Rachel (CS) involved early due to change-control and deployment complexity.
- Suggested internal contacts for follow-up: Connor O’Brien (Release Eng lead) for LTS policy language; Dr. Aisha Rahman / Hanae Suzuki for vuln response commitments; Bruno Silva for Private pinning mechanics.

Risk flags
- If we can’t commit to a clear LTS support window and security patch SLA in writing, procurement will likely stall.
- Data residency language needs to be precise (they will reject ambiguous cross-region failover wording).
